findings: The exact pikepdf wheel publishes a Microsoft Distributable Code License Summary and explicitly permits its distributors and external end users to copy/distribute that code subject to listed conditions.

The official full Visual Studio 2019 terms section4 allows its licensee to permit downstream distributors of its applications to copy Distributable Code as part of those applications. This is a possible upstream-program distribution chain, not proof that a host Visual Studio installation grants unrelated rights.
The Visual C++ Runtime2015-2022 end-user agreement permits install/use but expressly prohibits third-party redistribution or combination offerings. It is not itself a redistribution grant.

Final MSVC file/version origins must map to the relevant REDIST list and applicable upstream distribution permission. This review does not generalize pikepdf notice coverage to every CPython or Qt binary.

Significant primary application functionality, protective distributor/end-user terms, trademark restrictions and the distribution indemnity remain conditions. Exact final product terms and installer distribution evidence belong to PWS-0802; this internal unsigned stage does not prove that those conditions have been implemented.
msvc_license_review.scope_limit: No maintainer-owned Visual Studio license, credentials, commercial agreement, signature or global redistribution right is inferred.

pikepdf_runtime_identity.redistribution_list_mapping: Visual C++ Runtime Files includes unmodified files under [VisualStudioFolder]\VC\redist and subfolders, except debug_nonredist. The 2019 page has a directory rule, not an explicit msvcp140.dll filename entry.
pikepdf_runtime_identity.app_local_staging: Only this exact object retains its upstream-declared downstream distribution route; no generic grant for Qt/CPython/MSVC files.
